jobs.title: Commercial Strategy Senior Manager
jobs.description:
About Us:

Grow was born to tackle a critical challenge: making mental health care more effective and accessible for everyone. Since launching in 2020, 15 million sessions have started on Grow, and we've barely scratched the surface. We do it through a three-sided marketplace that empowers providers, augments insurance payors, and serves patients. Every solution we build reveals ten more waiting to be delivered, and that's just what gets us going. We've backed that ambition with more than $328M in funding, including our Series D at a $3B valuation from Sequoia Capital, Transformation Capital, TCV, SignalFire, Menlo Ventures, Goldman Sachs Alternatives, and others.

At Grow, the work you do can literally change someone's life. Your work here doesn't stay on a screen; it impacts whether someone can find, afford, and access quality care. That ambition sets us apart, and offers you an endless runway to impact one of the world's most urgent issues. We don’t have passenger seats here. Everyone is driving something that matters.

This work deserves real commitment. So if you thrive on meeting problems head on, untangling serious complexity, and working at pace with the sharpest yet kindest people around, you've come to the right place.

The Opportunity

Grow Therapy works with most of the largest health plans in the country. As those relationships have matured, the interesting question has shifted from whether a plan works with us to what we should build together, and there is no standard answer to that question.

This role owns a focused set of key relationships end to end. You decide what should be built with each plan, design the structure that delivers it, negotiate it, and stay with it once it is live.

The work runs on a multi-year horizon. You will spend real time with health plans’ senior executives, enough that they bring you problems before they have decided what to do about them.

You will work closely with our Director, Payor Strategy and our VP, Corporate and Business Development on a team small enough that each person carries a meaningful share of the company's strategy and influence to drive it.

What You'll Be Doing

Deciding what to build

 - Develop a point of view on each health plan you cover: where their behavioral health strategy is heading, what is not working, who owns the problem internally, and what would need to be true for them to commit to something ambitious.

 - Design the solution from first principles including economics, complex deal terms, directed volume, integrated referral pathways, co-developed clinical programs, risk-sharing. The right combination differs by plan, and in most cases it does not exist anywhere in the market.

 - Build the analytical case. Size the opportunity, model the economics, test the assumptions, and produce work that holds up to a health plan's strategy and finance teams.

 - Coordinate with Grow’s leadership. Work closely with our co-founders, operations, product, engineering, and finance to assist in the build, negotiation, and execution of the partnership.

Structuring and landing it

 - Lead the commercial structuring, including rate design, exclusivity mechanics, volume commitments, and performance economics, in direct conversation with health plan executives.

 - Build the relationships that make ambitious structures possible. Agreements of this scope are approved by a small number of senior people at each plan, and reaching them takes sustained time and credibility.

 - Bring Grow's operations, product, clinical, and finance teams into what you are designing, making the trade-offs required to turn a novel structure into something we can deliver.

Owning what it produces

 - Stay with the partnership after launch. Track how it is performing, work out why/when it is not, and use your relationships with health plan leaders to adjust the structure.

 - Apply what you learn in-market to the next structure, both with that plan and with the others you cover.

 - Feed what you learn back into Grow's product roadmap and long-range planning.

You'll Be a Good Fit If

 - You have three to seven years of experience in strategy consulting, corporate development, private equity, venture capital, or a strategy function at a high-growth company, with a record of strong performance.

 - You are comfortable with problems that have no established approach, and you tend to spend real time on how a problem is structured before solving it.

 - You want to see your work through. Designing the structure is the interesting part, and you also care about how it performs once it is in-market.

 - You can hold your own with senior external executives and build long-term relationships with them. You lead with the answer, and you build arguments that work on sophisticated audiences.

 - You think through second-order effects, including how a proposal lands across a health plan's network, actuarial, and clinical teams, and what it commits Grow to operationally.

 - You build the plan rather than asking for one.

 - Healthcare experience is helpful but not required.

Employment Type: Full Time, Exempt
Base Compensation: The base compensation range for this position is

Hybrid Commitment: $161,000–$215,000 USD Annually

Fully Remote Commitment: $134,000–$179,167 USD Annually 

This role can be hybrid (onsite from our NYC, San Francisco, or Seattle hub location three days per week: Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday) or fully remote. Both arrangements include travel 2–3 times per year (e.g., company and department offsites).
The base compensation for this role will vary depending on several factors, including relevant experience, qualifications, and the candidate’s working location.



Full Time Employee Benefits:

 - Health Benefits: Comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life, and disability coverage.

 - Grow for Grow: No cost access to therapy through the Grow platform (available to US employees)

 - Financial Wellness: Retirement savings programs and equity opportunities to help you invest in your future.

 - Flexible Time Off, Paid Holidays & Winter Break: Flexible time off, company paid holidays (which vary by country), and a full company wide Winter Break to rest and recharge

 - Parental Leave: Up to 18 weeks of paid parental leave to support you and your growing family and a new child stipend.

 - Mental Health Mornings/Afternoons: Dedicated weekly flexible time for self care, whether that's therapy, exercise, journaling, time with family, or simply taking a break.

 - Wellness & Development Stipend: Annual stipend to support your personal wellbeing and professional growth, from fitness and education to books and learning resources.

 - Commuter Benefits: Pre tax commuter benefits to support teammates working from one of our hub locations.

 - Home Office & Meals: Support for your home workspace plus meal benefits, with offerings tailored to both remote and hub based employees.

 - Additional Perks: A variety of wellbeing benefits, including wellness memberships, virtual care, pet insurance discounts (where available), and global travel assistance.

 - A Systems Thinker: You do not just run processes -- you think about why they exist and whether they are working. You can diagnose operational breakdowns, propose fixes, and implement them with limited oversight. You have strong intuitions about how planning, communication, and decision-making infrastructure should work at a scaling company.

 - A Strong Project Manager: You can build a project plan, manage complex timelines, coordinate across senior stakeholders, and ensure execution without losing sight of the objectives. Details do not fall through the cracks on your watch.

 - Comfortable with the Full Range of the Work: This role combines strategic process design with hands-on execution, including scheduling, logistics, and note-taking for executive meetings. You see both as part of the same job and do not minimize for the execution side.

 - A Senior Communicator: You are equally comfortable designing a facilitation agenda for an executive offsite and drafting a company-wide communication.  - AI-Forward: You actively use AI tools to improve your own productivity and the quality of the processes you run -- from automating coordination workflows to accelerating how information is synthesized and distributed. We're hiring a Commercial Finance & Operations Lead to build the operating backbone for two critical parts of our marketplace: Provider Recruitment & Experience and our PCP / EAP motion. Reporting to the Head of Revenue Operations, you'll partner closely with GTM leadership and Finance to translate strategy into executable plans, stand up the systems and workflows that run these businesses, and create the reporting and forecasting infrastructure leadership relies on to make decisions.

This is a hands-on, zero-to-one builder role. One week you might be designing a coverage model, the next you're rebuilding a forecasting workflow or helping leadership figure out where to invest capacity. In close partnership with the Head of Revenue Operations, you'll also be the driving force behind the data and AI foundation underneath Revenue Operations, architecting the core data layer that ties together Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, and Finance information, and helping shape how the function adopts AI going forward.




WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

 - Lead the execution of planning, forecasting, and pipeline management for Provider Recruitment & Experience and PCP / EAP, so leadership always has a reliable read on performance against targets.

 - Be the primary architect of the core data layer for Revenue Operations, connecting Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, and Finance information into a single reliable source of truth.

 - Help define the direction for how AI shows up in Revenue Operations, pinpointing where automation and AI tools can meaningfully improve GTM efficiency, forecasting, and decision-making.

 - Build and maintain the data models, pipelines, and analytics products that turn raw data into insight for everyone, from individual contributors to executives.

 - Design segmentation, coverage, and territory models, along with account allocation and capacity planning frameworks, for both lines of business.

 - Work closely with the Systems and Strategy & Operations teams so that data architecture, tooling, and process stay tightly aligned across RevOps.

 - Research, test, and roll out AI tools and vendors, keeping a pulse on the fast-moving AI landscape and turning new capabilities into practical use cases.

 - Put data governance, quality standards, and documentation practices in place that can scale as the organization grows.

 - Build dashboards and analyses that are ready for executive use and inform revenue strategy and company-wide reporting.

 - Act as a cross-functional quarterback across Operations, Commercial, Finance, and Product to keep the Revenue Strategy roadmap on track.

 - Build the playbooks, processes, and operating cadences needed to scale both businesses as they grow.

 - Champion a culture of building fast and iterating faster, favoring quick prototypes and rapid deployment over long, perfect build cycles.

 - Act as a thought partner to Revenue leadership on how AI and modern data infrastructure can shape the future of go-to-market operations.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Reduction in time-to-insight for revenue questions, measured by cycle time from request to delivered analysis.

 - Adoption of unified data models and dashboards across Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success teams.

 - Number of AI-driven use cases successfully piloted and deployed into production each quarter.

 - Improved forecast accuracy and reporting consistency across the revenue funnel.

 - Percentage of core revenue reporting migrated off manual/spreadsheet-based processes onto the unified data layer.


YOU’LL BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU HAVE

 - 7+ years in GTM Strategy & Operations, Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, FP&A / Strategic Finance, Business Operations, or a closely related function.

 - A track record of building commercial infrastructure from the ground up at an early-stage or rapidly scaling company.

 - Real hands-on technical ability: you're comfortable writing SQL and code yourself, designing data models, and building pipelines, not just directing others who do.

 - Fluency with the modern AI landscape and a track record of turning emerging tools into practical, production use cases.

 - Comfort moving between strategy, analysis, process design, and hands-on systems implementation. You're just as happy building a model as you are working through the details of a workflow.

 - Experience leading forecasting, territory planning, pipeline management, and executive business reviews.

 - Strong command of CRM platforms, BI tools, spreadsheets, and modern GTM systems.

 - Excellent judgment and cross-functional instincts, with an ability to turn messy information into clear decisions and scalable processes.
